notes: Governing documents for faculty leave: the Norman Campus Faculty Handbook (leaves policy 3.21, probationary period 3.7.3) and the Provost's Norman campus FMLA guidelines for faculty (dated 4/27/2015; the saved copy is a Wayback capture of 2018-04-04, inside the 2017-18 reference period; nothing suggests it was not in force on 2018-03-12). The HR FMLA page and FAQ (updated 01/25/2018) summarise FMLA for all employees. The Staff Handbook (updated 6/2/2017) governs staff; its provisions are coded with their staff groups.

No dedicated paid or unpaid parental, maternity or childbirth leave exists for faculty in the saved documents. Faculty rely on FMLA (12 workweeks unpaid), with their own extended sick leave used concurrently, plus the Provost's Modified Duties (teaching relief for the FMLA semester, discretionary relief in the following semester) and FMLA-based tenure-clock extension.

Birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1, own extended sick leave c2 within it) within the semester of Modified Duties (c5, relief for the portion of the semester not covered by FMLA) -> discretionary Modified Duties in the semester immediately following (c7); c6 (redistributed teaching) is in lieu of c5.

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1) within the semester of Modified Duties (c5) -> discretionary Modified Duties in the following semester (c7); c6 in lieu of c5. (c2 is own-illness leave, birth parent only.)
Modified Duties pay: the guidelines keep 'full time employment' but state no pay level; full pay inferred and flagged under R3 on c5 and c7.

Faculty Handbook 3.21.4: 12-month faculty extended sick leave and paid leave are in 'the University's Paid Leave and Extended Sick Leave Policy', and 3.21 refers to the Regents' Policy Manual for additional leave information; neither is saved. The Staff Handbook's PTO and ESL text (c14, c15) may be that policy as applied to staff; 12-month faculty are not the standard (academic-year) appointment.

Short- and long-term disability coverage: listed among University-sponsored benefit programmes; the employee pays in full for all insurance other than dental, life, AD&D and shared medical; no benefit terms in the saved documents (plan documents not saved).

Not components (cannot be used for a birth or adoption): sabbatical leave (professional development, six years of service), administrative leave (University's interest), fellowship leave, political-campaign leave, jury duty, voting, military leave, bone marrow/organ donation leave, disciplinary and investigative leave, phased retirement (age 55 and ten years).

FMLA staff text (Staff Handbook 3.11.2) gives 12 weeks to each spouse employed by the University and requires birth/adoption leave to be taken consecutively; the HR FMLA page names Staff Handbook 3.11.2 as the policy. Recorded as c1's dual_employee_rule; it does not change any figure.

Documents cited but not saved: University of Oklahoma Regents' Policy Manual (Leave Policy); the University's Paid Leave and Extended Sick Leave Policy (12-month faculty); short- and long-term disability plan documents (Sooner Options); academic unit faculty absence policies (Faculty Handbook 4.19); college teaching-load policies (3.16.1); FMLA request and certification forms (HR page).
